key_insight: Applying classic supervised ML models (KNN, LDA, QDA, Gaussian Process) together with class-imbalance mitigation improves predictive capability for dementia using routine patient health data, enabling more reliable early-warning signals.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of accurately predicting dementia from heterogeneous, imbalanced healthcare data where minority (dementia) cases are underrepresented and traditional models may be biased or unstable.
method: Assemble and preprocess patient health records and clinical features relevant to cognitive decline.
Train and compare supervised classifiers: K-Nearest Neighbors, Linear/Quadratic Discriminant Analysis, and Gaussian Process Classifier.
Mitigate class imbalance (e.g., resampling or class-weighting strategies) and evaluate models with robust metrics to improve minority-class detection.
impact: Provides a practical, reproducible pipeline showing that combining interpretable classical models with imbalance-aware training can boost dementia prediction reliability—useful guidance for ML practitioners building clinical decision-support tools.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: data → preprocessing → imbalance handling → model training → evaluation
Performance comparison chart (bar/line) of classifiers on key metrics like recall, precision, and AUC
Before/after class distribution visualization to show impact of imbalance mitigation
ROC/precision-recall curves or a confusion-matrix icon to emphasize minority-class detection
paper_title: Predictive Analytics for Dementia: Machine Learning on Healthcare Data
paper_authors: Shafiul Ajam Opee, Nafiz Fahad, Anik Sen, Rasel Ahmed, Fariha Jahan
